Its section 2(b) provides, in the held text, that "The organizations listed herein are terminated" and lists the Council for Urban Affairs established by this order, naming it by its Executive order number and date; its section 3 provides that "This order shall be effective July 1,1970." Terminated by Executive Order 11541, signed July 1, 1970 (35 FR 10737, Federal Register of July 2, 1970). Its section 2(b) provides, in the held text, that "The organizations listed herein are terminated" and lists the Council for Urban Affairs established by this order, naming it by its Executive order number and date; its section 3 provides that "This order shall be effective July 1,1970." The termination of the Council is whole-body, not partial, and the functions heretofore assigned to the listed organizations are to be performed by the Domestic Council; the first end of every clause below is therefore July 1, 1970. This clause is section 1(c), which composes the Council of the Vice President, the Attorney General, the Secretaries of Agriculture, Commerce, Labor, Health, Education, and Welfare, Housing and Urban Development and Transportation, and such other heads of departments and agencies as the President may from time to time direct. It ended with the Council on the same date: it has no application once the Council it creates, staffs or constrains no longer exists, and no held source shows it continuing independently. Later events recorded on this clause: Executive Order 11500 (signed December 12, 1969; 34 FR 19701, Federal Register of December 16, 1969) amended section 1(c) of this order before the termination by deleting its closing words that other heads of departments and agencies as the President may from time to time direct are members and inserting the same words with the words "and others" added after the words departments and agencies, so that the President could also direct persons who are not heads of departments or agencies to serve (before: other heads of departments and agencies as directed; after: other heads of departments and agencies and others as directed); it is an amendment and not an end. Executive Order 12553 (signed February 25, 1986) later revoked this order by number in its table, listing it with the subject "Establishing the Council for Urban Affairs"; because the Council had been terminated on July 1, 1970, that revocation came after the first end and is not it.

research_rationale:
Identity: the held Federal Register text (34 FR 1223, the issue of January 25, 1969) is Executive Order 11452, Establishing the Council for Urban Affairs, dated January 23, 1969. I read the whole order; the representation is the machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF (OCR for this period), and I did not inspect the page images. End: Executive Order 11541 section 2(b), effective July 1, 1970 under its section 3, which terminates the Council for Urban Affairs by naming this order; this is an earlier end than the provisional status's express revocation by Executive Order 12553 (1986-02-25), which is recorded as a later event. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog, each marked complete in the dossier; the U.S. Code search found editorial notes (under 42 U.S.C. 3531 and 31 U.S.C. 501) that recite both the termination by Executive Order 11541 and the revocation by Executive Order 12553, which I read as leads and did not rely on for the ending.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"The order states no end date and no termination clause of its own. The earliest ending found is Executive Order 11541 section 2(b), effective July 1, 1970 (signing date July 1, 1970; its section 3 states the effective date). A held-text search for this order's number found no earlier revoking, superseding or terminating instrument; Executive Order 11500 only amends section 1(c) and Executive Order 12553 came later.","independent_command_check":"No command of this order operates apart from the Council: the composition, presiding, advisory functions, executive secretary, staff support and construction clause all depend on the body the order establishes. Executive Order 11541 section 2(b) provides that the functions heretofore assigned to the terminated organizations are performed by the Domestic Council, so the functions did not continue as commands of this order.","savings_check":"Executive Order 11541 was read in full. Its only saving provision, section 1(b), covers actions of the Bureau of the Budget and its Director and does not reach the Council for Urban Affairs or this order; section 2(b) states no exception or saving for the Council. The later revocation by Executive Order 12553 came after the Council had been terminated and has no bearing on the first end.","scope_check":"Fifteen clauses are inventoried by correction, covering the title and enacting clause with section 1(a), section 1(b) and (c), the section 2 lead and its eight numbered directions, section 3(a) and (b) and section 4. Executive Order 11541 terminates the Council as a whole, not in part. I read sections 3(b) and 4 as ending with the Council because they staff and constrain the Council and have no subject without it; that reading is disclosed."}

savings.reason: Executive Order 11541, read in full (3,633 characters), has one saving provision, section 1(b), which keeps outstanding delegations, rules, regulations, orders, circulars, bulletins and other executive or administrative action issued or taken by or relating to the Bureau of the Budget or its Director in force, until amended or revoked, as if they related to the Office of Management and Budget. That provision is limited to Bureau of the Budget actions and does not reach the Council for Urban Affairs or this order. Section 2(b) terminates the listed organizations, including the Council for Urban Affairs, outright and provides that their functions are to be performed by the Domestic Council; it states no exception or saving for the Council or its acts. Nothing shows any command of this order continuing after July 1, 1970.
